items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1958-06-19, 20
items.q: Oh yeah I played around there with him on jobs, you know, a little gig job some time. I played with him in Alexandria.

ctx.x: Do you think that Brunk imitated Buddy Petite?

No he didn't imitate, he was a better cornet player in Buddy Petite I think. Brunk was a better cornet player than Buddy Petite. He knew a little something about music you see. Uh huh. And Buddy didn't know nothing about music. That made Brunk the best. Did you ever play in the same band with Bunk any place? Oh yeah I played around there with him on jobs, you know, a little gig job some time. I played with him in Alexandria. And got a job for him, got a job for him and Clarence William and Paul, a fellow with…
The violin? Wasn't he with Handy once too?

items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1960-05-10
items.q: That was Bunk Johnson's uncle. ... Yeah, Bunk, his uncle was named Willie Young.

ctx.x: Yeah. He played by Bronk Johnson playing the trumpet. And Harry Walker in Alexander. Well, they had some different bands around there. You know, they all played the Red Book. We was all connected together, you see. We had a big orchestra used to rehearse every Sunday. We just rehearsed over to them. And we'd invite all the musicians to that rehearsal, you know, a bunch of men. Every Sunday, there was Baby Lovey. he was a drummer. He was in Kansas City now, with Lee's band. And they had some bands around there,…
